full_text:
Southern Odisha likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on November 3 and 4; system expected to cross Andhra Pradesh coast on November 3
Bhubaneswar: Even as Odisha is recovering from the impact of Cyclone Arnab, another weather system, Cyclone Murasu, is threatening to bring heavy rainfall to several parts of the State, particularly southern Odisha, over the next few days.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange warning for five southern districts — Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri — forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 3 and 4.
Although Murasu is not expected to make a direct landfall in Odisha, its indirect impact is likely to trigger widespread rainfall and thunderstorms in the State as the system moves towards the south Andhra Pradesh coast.
According to the IMD forecast, Cyclone Murasu is likely to intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal on Monday and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narasapur by the morning of November 3. Wind speeds during landfall are expected to reach 100-110 kmph, with gusts up to 120 kmph.
The weather system is likely to influence weather conditions in Odisha from Sunday. Several places in the State may experience light to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. The IMD has already issued a yellow warning for thunderstorms and rain in 16 districts.
On Monday, southern Odisha is likely to receive light to moderate rainfall, with heavy rainfall of 7 cm to 12 cm expected at isolated places in Ganjam and Gajapati districts. Thunderstorms and lightning are also likely in several coastal and southern districts.
The situation may intensify on November 3 and 4, when heavy to very heavy rainfall is forecast in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts. Heavy rainfall is also likely at isolated places in Nabarangpur, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Nayagarh, Khordha and Puri districts on November 3.
On November 4, the rainfall activity is likely to continue, with heavy rainfall forecast in Nuapada, Nayagarh, Puri, Khordha, Bolangir and Bargarh districts, besides the five southern districts under the orange warning.
The IMD has advised people to keep track of weather updates, take shelter during thunderstorms to avoid lightning strikes and follow traffic advisories in urban areas.
Meanwhile, rainfall activity is expected to gradually decline from November 5, although some places may continue to experience light to moderate rain and thunderstorms. The intensity is likely to reduce considerably on November 6 and 7.
The latest weather development has put the southern districts of Odisha on alert, particularly in view of the recent experience with Cyclone Arnab.

Deep Depression Intensifies Into Severe Cyclone Murasu; IMD Issues Yellow Alert For Coastal Andhra
It is expected to cross the south coastal areas between Nellore and Narsapur by the morning of November 3, with wind speeds of 100–110 kmph.
Amaravati: The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a Yellow Alert for the coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm, Murasu (Tamil name for drum), on Sunday.
The system is expected to cross the south coastal areas of the state between Nellore and Narsapur by the morning of November 3, with wind speeds of 100–110 kmph and gusts up to 120 kmph.
"Deep Depression intensified into Cyclonic Storm 'Murasu' over Southwest and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 11:30 am on November 1," the IMD shared in an X post.

At 5.30 am on Sunday, the system was centred over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, approximately 700 km east-southeast of Chennai, 770 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 770 km southeast of Machilipatnam.
Moving west-northwestwards at a speed of 23 kmph, the system is expected to continue in the same direction before approaching the Andhra coast.
The IMD has warned of damage to thatched and kutcha houses, rooftops, power and communication poles, along with the possibility of uprooted trees and damaged plantations.

Extremely Heavy Rainfall Alert
The approaching system is likely to bring heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across several states in southern and eastern India. Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall at a few places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 2 and 3. Heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places on November 4, the IMD said.
Rayalaseema may experience heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 2 and 3. Telangana is likely to receive heavy rainfall on November 2, followed by heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 3.
South Odisha is also likely to receive heavy rainfall on November 2, with heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 3 and 4.

Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu may receive heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 2 and 3. South Chhattisgarh is also likely to experience heavy rainfall on November 2 and heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 3.
Winds May Reach 120 Kmph
The IMD has warned that wind speeds over the west-central Bay of Bengal could reach 100–110 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 120 kmph, from the night of November 2 until the afternoon of November 3.
Similar wind conditions are expected along the Andhra Pradesh coast during this period. Squally weather is also likely along the north Tamil Nadu-Puducherry coast. Sea conditions are expected to become high to very high over parts of the west-central Bay of Bengal and along the Andhra Pradesh coast, making fishing and movement of small vessels unsafe.
Advice for Fishermen
The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the southeast Bay of Bengal on November 1 and 2, and the southwest Bay of Bengal until the morning of November 4.

Fishing activities have also been restricted along the Andhra Pradesh coast from the morning of November 2 until the afternoon of November 4.
Similar warnings have been issued for the west-central Bay of Bengal, north Tamil Nadu-Puducherry coast and south Odisha coast.
Flooding, Devastation Likely
The met department has warned of localised flooding, waterlogging in low-lying areas, disruption of road and rail traffic, and riverine and coastal flooding. Landslides are also possible in hilly areas.
Strong winds may damage vulnerable houses, uproot trees and affect standing crops, particularly banana, papaya and coconut plantations.
The IMD has advised authorities to suspend fishing operations, shift residents of vulnerable coastal settlements to safer locations and regulate road and rail traffic wherever necessary. People in affected areas have been advised to remain indoors, avoid vulnerable structures and follow official weather advisories.
Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Narsapur in the early hours of October 28, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph.
It claimed seven lives and caused widespread damage to crops, roads, electricity and telecom infrastructure in the coastal districts. Crops over thousands of acres were damaged in the cyclone, while hundreds of electricity poles and trees were uprooted.

title: Tamil Nadu Orange Alert Issued as Murasu Storm Nears Coast - Urban Acres

full_text:
Tamil Nadu has issued an orange alert for Tiruvallur as the Murasu storm over the Bay of Bengal is expected to bring extremely heavy rainfall, while five districts are likely to receive heavy rain, according to a report by Dinamalar citing the weather centre.
The report said the storm is centred over the south-western and west-central Bay of Bengal. It is forecast to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur in the early hours of November 3.
Tiruvallur was placed under an orange alert for November 1 because of the possibility of extremely heavy rainfall. An orange alert indicates the need for heightened preparedness in areas that could face intense rain and related disruption.
The report also said that districts in Tamil Nadu were expected to receive heavy rainfall, classified under a yellow alert, on November 2. It separately stated that extremely heavy rainfall was possible in some districts on November 2. However, the supplied report does not list the names of all the districts covered by these alerts.
The weather system is significant for the Chennai metropolitan region and surrounding urban areas because intense rainfall can affect roads, low-lying neighbourhoods, drainage networks and daily travel. Tiruvallur lies within the wider urban and industrial belt north-west of Chennai, where rainfall conditions can have implications beyond district boundaries.
For November 3, the report identified the Nilgiris as a district likely to receive heavy rainfall under a yellow alert. The forecast categories and dates were attributed to the weather centre in the report.
The next key milestone is the storm’s expected coastal crossing between Nellore and Narsapur in the early hours of November 3. Further district-specific warnings and operational instructions would determine the local preparedness measures required in affected areas.
